subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should gateway/security owners accept this PR's combination of schema caps, shape pre-checks, and a device-signature per-IP lockout as the intended pre-auth mitigation once current-head proof is supplied?
rationale: The diff changes unauthenticated Gateway auth and protocol validation; tests show mechanics, but maintainer intent is needed for the fail-closed limits and lockout behavior.

options.title: Accept after current-head proof
options.body: Require live or terminal proof from f20a530d showing the schema cap, pre-crypto lockout, and canonical AUTH_RATE_LIMITED response, then proceed with owner review.

options.title: Narrow or split the hardening
options.body: Ask the author to split protocol bounds, helper shape checks, or the rate-limit gate if owners want smaller security-review units.

options.title: Replace the mitigation shape
options.body: Close or pause this branch if owners prefer a different pre-auth policy, such as a broader shared handshake limiter or different protocol bounds.

recommendation.title: Accept after current-head proof
recommendation.body: Require live or terminal proof from f20a530d showing the schema cap, pre-crypto lockout, and canonical AUTH_RATE_LIMITED response, then proceed with owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: The reviewed history ties the device-auth handshake surface most strongly to steipete's earlier device auth and helper extraction work.
